items.title: Foucault's panopticon
items.claim: Michel Foucault's Discipline and Punish (1975) used what 18th-century architectural design to illustrate modern power?
items.reveal_title: Bentham's never-built prison became a model of modern surveillance
items.reveal:
Bentham proposed the panopticon in 1791 as a circular building where inmates could be observed at any moment without knowing when.

Foucault argued the principle, the internalisation of an unseen watcher, had spread to schools, factories and clinics.
items.why: Power in modernity, Foucault argued, often works through visibility rather than coercion.

items.title: UK household structure today
items.claim: What proportion of UK households in 2022 were single-person households according to the Office for National Statistics?
items.reveal_title: Roughly three in ten UK households are one person
items.reveal:
ONS data for 2022 reported around 30% of households contained a single person. The figure has risen steadily since the 1960s.

The 'standard' nuclear family is now a minority household type.
items.why: Demographic change reshapes assumptions built into policy and earlier sociological theory.

items.title: Oakley's domestic labour finding
items.claim: Ann Oakley's The Sociology of Housework (1974) interviewed 40 London housewives. What did most report about housework?

options.text: It was monotonous, low-status and isolating
It was equally shared with husbands
It was paid at market rates

items.reveal:
Oakley reported 70% of respondents expressed dissatisfaction. Her work established housework as a legitimate object of sociological study.

Later 'second shift' research (Hochschild, 1989) extended the analysis to employed women.
items.why: Recognising unpaid labour as work reframed measurements of economic activity.
